# v0.9.0b1 — Fewer entities, wallbox events

Beta of the integration and the app **0.9.0b1**. The app update only renames
its sidebar entry to **Modbus RTU**; the integration also works with app 0.8.2.

- **Breaking: fewer entities, more attributes.** Each sensor answers one
  question; what only details it is now one of its attributes. 32 entities
  are removed (and cleaned from the registry on the first start): the raw
  EVSE/CP states ride on **Charging status**, the error code and category on
  **Error**, heartbeat health on **Connection quality**, the phase voltages on
  **Total power**, the session duration, maximum current and count on
  **Session energy**, the due time on **Pending change**, the planned start on
  **Timed charging status**, the switched phases on **Requested phases**, the
  downgrade current on **Downgrade active**, the fallback mode and current on
  **Energy manager fallback active**. The installation values (DIP switches
  and service tool) are the attributes of the new **Wallbox settings**
  diagnostic sensor. Every remaining sensor is enabled by default and nothing
  new compiles statistics. Re-select the inputs of automations made from the
  bundled blueprints; templates read `state_attr()` instead of the removed
  entity. See [Updating to 0.9.0](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-mennekes-amtron/blob/v0.9.0b1/docs/upgrading.md#updating-to-090).

- **New event entity Wallbox event:** what the wallbox changed on its own,
  as the counterpart to **Control result**, which reports your commands. It
  reports a car plugged in or unplugged (with the energy and duration of the
  session), a charge started or stopped, a fault that appeared or cleared
  (with code and category), an RFID authorization or rejection, a downgrade,
  a cable lock and a phase switch. Only a change between two known readings
  creates an event; a start, a reload or a lost connection sets a baseline
  and reports nothing. Enabled by default; it records only those changes.

- **BavarianData's Charging Cable sensor** is now the first cable source for
  automatic selection and Virtual Plug & Charge: from BavarianData 0.9.30 it
  carries BMW's time for the plug state and names the reading behind it, so
  it proves a fresh plug-in for every car. An older BavarianData works as before.
